body.html: William Blair is a global partnership with expertise in investment banking, investment management and private wealth management. In a professional setting of this kind, meeting rooms, desks and reception areas are places where the brand is experienced in everyday use. SFP received a direct commission for personalised leather office accessories. The starting point is significant: William Blair supplied its own design inspiration. SFP was therefore not asked to invent an unrelated visual language, but to understand an existing idea and translate it into physical objects.

The particular challenge was one of translation: shape, leather, colour, edges and branding needed to reflect the supplied reference while becoming a clear specification that could be made. Office pieces are seen at close quarters and handled often. Tactility, controlled proportions and an appropriately scaled mark therefore matter more than decorative complexity.

The client’s visual inspiration provided a shared reference for the discussion. SFP used it to define the leather pieces and their personalisation. In a process of this kind, an image or moodboard has to be broken down into reviewable decisions: which proportions carry the idea, which surface creates the intended character, how will a blind deboss behave in the selected leather, and where should it sit on the object? Where several pieces are involved, recurring characteristics need defining without obscuring their individual functions.

William Blair received more than a written interpretation of the brief: it received personalised leather objects that carried its own inspiration into the working environment. That is the specific value of SFP’s role. A visual direction was refined until it could become tangible, branded products. The restrained deboss allows identity and material to work together, which suits a professional setting where details should be present without becoming loud. Instead, the case demonstrates a clear division of expertise: the client supplied the creative idea, and SFP made it practicable as a product.
